baseline_requirements: Remote is powered by a non-rechargeable battery (agreed in previous meeting)
Remote is powered by a hybrid system: kinetic power with a battery as backup (kinetic does not charge the battery)
Battery must be long-lasting so users do not recharge every few days; remote needs a battery even if an alternative source is used
Target group is people aged 15 to 35
Functions are grouped into categories (audio-visual and others) on the remote
Remote controls the TV only; ignore teletext and other functions
Product incorporates the corporate colour and slogan
Slogan appears on the casing (e.g. on the side)
Remote incorporates a logo on the casing
Style and fancy look and feel are the top design priority, with innovation shown in look and feel rather than extra functions
Easy to use and user friendly throughout, while still having technology
Not shaped like a literal fruit (no apple, no lemon shape); fruit trend only inspires texture and colour
Soft, spongy, ergonomic, friendly-to-handle materials; plastic textured to feel soft and grippy; rubber may be incorporated into the case
Case combines plastic with rubber on the outside for a warm, comfortable feel and curved shapes
No wood or titanium case, since they force a boxy rectangular shape
Use vibrant natural colours with softness in materials, shape and function
Possible lemon/lime theme with green or yellow colours (idea only, not agreed)
Lighting feature: buttons light up when touched or picked up (possibly in different colours), usable in the dark
Case could be slightly transparent and tinted yellow, with one or two low-power lights glowing subtly in the dark
Interchangeable covers sold with the control in different looks
Take some iPod features (high-tech, few buttons) but softer, more vibrant and friendly rather than hard and glossy
Buttons are large, easy and comfortable to press, not tiny
Buttons are rubber and not big protruding; more flush with the case
Stand-by button is always red
Volume up and down buttons are clearly distinguishable from each other
Use a very bright colour if the corporate scheme allows, so the control is easy to find and not tacky; avoid dark colours
Yellow must feature in the colour scheme; yellow background with bold contrasting button colour
Only basic, frequently used functions are visible on the front; advanced, rarely used functions are hidden inside
If voice activation is included, a button alternative must always exist, possibly in the hidden section
Remote does not look like a big square block; not flat or angular, but curvy
No voice talk-back to the user (no spoken slogan or speaker output)
Remote is comfortable to hold, attractive, not easily lost, and feels right in the hand
Remote is small and slim but not so small it is hard to use
Snowman shape: larger lower part sits in the hand, smaller bubble at top for other functions (team agreed)
Remote may fold up to reveal a third group of controls inside, with volume controls on the body
No LCD display (cost and complexity, no input to feed it)
Jog dial for volume and channel control, placed where it fits the device shape, considering hand position and accidental movement
Number buttons are still needed for skipping many channels, even with a jog dial
baseline_decisions: Presentations in order (Andrew, Craig, David), discussion at the end, then decisions
Pursue one unifying theme across shape, materials and series as marketing identity, linked to yellow company colour and fruit such as lime/lemon, to be agreed in production-side discussion
Next meeting in thirty minutes, with designers working with Play-doh meanwhile
Meeting goal is to reach a decision on the product concept; about fifteen minutes remained
Corporate colour appears to be yellow, possibly constraining colour choice (unconfirmed)
Keep component count low (affects cost, complexity, size, time to market)
Rubber case cannot be combined with a solar power source
Titanium case cannot be curved (must be square)
Wood case cannot be curved; plastic has no restrictions
LCD panel or scroll wheel needs more complicated logic; buttons are standard
